==English==

===Etymology===
From {{inh|en|enm|otherwise}}, {{m|enm|othre wise}}, from {{inh|en|ang|on ōþre wīsan|lit=in (on) other/different manner}}; equivalent to {{suffix|en|other|wise}}. Compare {{cog|fy|yn oarwei|t=otherwise}}, {{cog|is|öðruvísi|t=different}}.

===Pronunciation===
* {{IPA|en|/ˈʌð.əˌwaɪz/|a=UK}}
* {{IPA|en|/ˈʌð.ɚˌwaɪz/|a=GA}}
* {{audio|en|en-us-otherwise.ogg|a=US}}

===Adverb===
{{en-adv|-}}

# {{lb|en|manner}} Differently, in another way.
#: {{syn|en|elsewise}}
#: {{ant|en|q1=in the same way|likewise|thuswise|;|q3=in no way whatsoever|nohow|in no way|not at all|by no means}}
#: {{nearsyn|en|contrarily|contrastingly}}
#: {{ux|en|You may have a point, but I think '''otherwise'''.}}
#: {{ux|en|Do you want the newest items put up top, or do you want it done '''otherwise'''?}}
#: {{ux|en|Could I do '''otherwise''' than smile?}}
#: {{ux|en|It is not permitted to sell or '''otherwise''' distribute any copies.}}
#* {{RQ:King James Version|1 Timothy|6|3|passage=If any man teach '''otherwise''', and consent not to wholesome words, euen the wordes of our Lord Iesus Christ, and to the doctrine which is according to godlinesse:}}
#* '''1927-29''', {{w|Mahatma Gandhi|M.K. Gandhi}}, ''{{w|The Story of My Experiments with Truth}}'', translated '''1940''' by {{w|Mahadev Desai}}, [https://www.mkgandhi.org/autobio/chap03.htm Part I, Chapter iii]:
#*: Much as I wish that I had not to write this chapter, I know that I shall have to swallow many such bitter draughts in the course of this narrative. And I cannot do '''otherwise''', if I claim to be a worshipper of Truth. {{...}}
#* {{quote-web|en|year=2011|author=Phil McNulty|title=Euro 2012: Montenegro 2-2 England|site=news.bbc.co.uk|url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/15195384.stm
|passage=Fabio Capello insisted Rooney was in the right frame of mind to play in stormy Podgorica despite his father's arrest on Thursday in a probe into alleged betting irregularities, but his flash of temper - when he kicked out at Miodrag Dzudovic - suggested '''otherwise'''.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20120110193113/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/15195384.stm|archivedate=10 January 2012}}
# {{lb|en|conjunctive}} In different [[circumstance]]s; [[or else]].
#: {{syn|en|elsewise}}
#: {{ux|en|I’m not well today, '''otherwise''' I would have helped.}}
#: {{ux|en|You have to open your umbrella, '''otherwise''' you'll get wet.}}
#* {{RQ:Jefferies Amateur Poacher|chapter=1|passage=They burned the old gun that used to stand in the dark corner up in the garret, close to the stuffed fox that always grinned so fiercely. Perhaps the reason why he seemed in such a ghastly rage was that he did not come by his death fairly. '''Otherwise''' his pelt would not have been so perfect. And why else was he put away up there out of sight?—and so magnificent a brush as he had too.}}
#* {{RQ:Churchill Celebrity|chapter=IV|page=46|passage=No matter how early I came down, I would find him on the veranda, smoking cigarettes, or '''otherwise''' his man would be there with a message to say that his master would shortly join me if I would kindly wait.}}
#* {{quote-journal|en|year=2012|month=March-April|author=[[w:Terry Sejnowski|Terrence J. Sejnowski]]
|volume=100|issue=2|page=171|magazine=w:American Scientist
|title=[http://www.americanscientist.org/bookshelf/pub/well-connected-brains Well-connected Brains]
|passage=Creating a complete map of the human connectome would therefore be a monumental milestone but not the end of the journey to understanding how our brains work. The achievement will transform neuroscience and serve as the starting point for asking questions we could not '''otherwise''' have answered,{{nb...}}.}}
# {{lb|en|conjunctive}} In all other respects; apart from that; except for this.
#: {{syn|en|elsewise}}
#: {{ux|en|He lost his temper once in a while. '''Otherwise''' he behaved rationally.}}
#: {{ux|en|There was one rotten apple in an '''otherwise''' perfect batch.}}
#* {{quote-journal|en|date=1 September 2013|author=Phil McNulty|url=http://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/0/football/23830980|journal=BBC Sport
|passage=Robin van Persie squandered United's best chance late on but '''otherwise''' it was a relatively comfortable afternoon for Liverpool's new goalkeeper Simon Mignolet, who has yet to concede a Premier League goal since his £9m summer move from Sunderland.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150325063804/http://www.bbc.co.uk:80/sport/0/football/23830980|archivedate=25 March 2015}}

====Usage notes====
* "Otherwise" is often used to refer to the negative of something. The something may be a noun phrase, a verb phrase, an adjective phrase, an adverb phrase, a clause, or even something larger.

====Derived terms====
{{col|en
|otherwiseness
|otherwise engaged
|until proven otherwise
}}
